create_game.description: Start a new game on your Spawn account, named as you like and begun from one of Spawn's starters (3D, 2D, a UI game or voxels), and get back its world id and play link, ready for 'Send a message to Savi' to have Savi build something in it. Spawn picks the engine a new game runs on. A workflow can't delete a game, so delete one you no longer want in Spawn.
create_game.name: create_game

parameters.description: The game's name. It also makes the game's @ address, so it can't be the name of another of your games. Leave blank and Spawn names it game-2, game-3 and so on.

parameters.description: The skeleton the new game starts as: pick the one nearest the game you have in mind. Savi, or your own changes, build on it.
parameters.name: starter

name.description: The game's name. Creating or getting a game gives it as it was written; the list of games gives the form its link uses, like sky-garden.

play_url.description: The link to play the game.

uses_git.description: Whether the game's code is a git repository (Spawn 6).

world_id.description: The game's world id, which the other Spawn steps take.

get_game.description: Look up one of your games by its name, @ address, play link or world id, and get its play link, its engine version and, for a Spawn 6 game, the address of the git repository its code lives in.

get_game_spec.description: Get a game's saved spec: its whole definition, as data. Read the latest draft, the version players see, an earlier version by number, or a published update by name. Useful for keeping a copy, or for checking whether a game has changed since a workflow last looked. A Spawn 6 game's code is a git repository, and Spawn reads the spec out of it.
get_game_spec.name: get_game_spec

parameters.description: The game: pick one of yours, or give its @ address (like @you/my-game), its play link or its world id.
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: 'draft' for the latest saved version, 'published' for the one players see, a version number, or the name of a published update (the end of its play link).

note.description: Why there is no spec, when not found.

list_rooms.description: See a game's live rooms and how many players are in each. A room runs only while someone is in the game, so no rooms means nobody is playing right now. It can wait for someone to join first, for example after sending a player the game's link.

parameters.name: game

parameters.description: How long to wait for someone to join when nobody is playing, checking every ten seconds. If nobody joins in time the step still succeeds, with 'live' false. Leave at 0 to look once.

message_savi.description: Post a message into a game's studio chat, where Savi, Spawn's AI game builder, reads it. Sent as a task, Savi takes the work on and can split it across up to eight of her own sub-agents; sent as a note, it is context for her next turn. Nothing comes back: no reply, acknowledgement or word that she has finished, so look for the change in the game itself. Only a connection made from a person's own Spawn account can message Savi; Spawn turns an agent account away.

mock_response.message:
Please take this on: Add a leaderboard next to the spawn point.

Fan it out across your sub-agents if it splits cleanly. This came from a Lodol workflow, which can't read a reply, so just push as each piece lands.

message_savi.name: message_savi

parameters.description: The game: pick one of yours, or give its @ address (like @you/my-game), its play link or its world id.
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: What to tell Savi, as you would in the studio chat. For a task, describe the result broadly rather than as a list of steps: splitting it up is what Savi's sub-agents are good at.

parameters.name: message

parameters.description: A task asks Savi to do the work. A note is only context: Savi reads it, and does nothing about it unless asked.

options.label: Ask Savi to take it on

run_script.description: Run a short piece of read-only JavaScript in a game's live room and get back what it returns: how many players are in, where an object is, what a scoreboard holds. The script can look but not change anything. It needs someone in the game: when nobody is, it doesn't run, and comes back with 'live' false. A script that throws fails the step with Spawn's error.
run_script.display_name: Run a script in a live game
run_script.name: run_script

parameters.description: The game: pick one of yours, or give its @ address (like @you/my-game), its play link or its world id.
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: JavaScript that returns a value, using the game's own api. 'Get a game's building guide' has the reference.

examples.label: List some objects
examples.value: return api.query({}).slice(0, 20).map(o => ({ id: o.id, tags: o.tags }))

parameters.name: script

note.description: Why nothing was read, when nobody is in the game; else empty.

result.description: What the script returned: a number, text, true or false, a list or an object.

upload_file.description: Put a 3D model (.glb), a texture or a sound on Spawn's CDN for a game, and get back the address it is served from and the /cdn/ path the game's code uses for it: use it in the game, or hand it to Savi, say to use an image an earlier AI step made as a texture. The file can be uploaded, come from an earlier step, or be fetched from a public address.
upload_file.display_name: Upload a file to a game
upload_file.name: upload_file

parameters.description: The game: pick one of yours, or give its @ address (like @you/my-game), its play link or its world id.
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: The file: upload one, pick one from an earlier step, or give a public address to fetch it from.
parameters.name: file

parameters.description: The file's name with its extension, like knight.glb, which tells Spawn what kind of file it is. Spawn serves every file under a name made from its contents, so only the extension is used. Leave blank to use the file's own name.
parameters.name: file_name

already_there.description: Whether the same file was uploaded before, so nothing new was stored.

cdn_path.description: What the game's code refers to the file by, /cdn/ and its name.

file_name.description: The name the file came with.

name.description: The name Spawn serves the file under, made from its contents.

response.description: Spawn's answer to the upload, as it came.

url.description: The address the file is served from.

description: Make and run multiplayer 3D games on Spawn from a workflow. Hand Savi, Spawn's AI game builder, a task in plain words; start new games; see who is playing and read each live room's log; run read-only scripts against a game while it runs; upload models, textures and sounds; and keep a copy of any game's spec.
